clip_ratio.description: Limits how much the model policy changes in a single update. Values that are too high cause instability, and values that are too low slow learning.
clip_ratio.hint: Must be a value between 0.1 and 1.5

clip_ratio_high.description: Sets the maximum allowed increase in token probability per update for positive-advantage tokens. Higher values allow more aggressive policy changes but may reduce output diversity.
clip_ratio_high.hint: Must be a value between 0.0 and 0.5

clip_ratio_low.description: Sets the maximum allowed decrease in token probability per update for negative-advantage tokens. Lower values promote exploration and help prevent the model from converging too quickly.
clip_ratio_low.hint: Must be a value between 0.0 and 0.5

global_batch_size.description: Total number of training samples processed per optimizer step. Larger values improve training stability but use more memory.
global_batch_size.hint: Choose from the available batch size options

judge_model_id.description: Bedrock model ID used as the judge for RLAIF evaluation

kl_loss_coef.description: Controls how closely the model stays to its original behavior during training. Higher values constrain changes more, and lower values allow the model to drift further.
kl_loss_coef.hint: Must be a value between 0 and 0.1

learning_rate.description: Step size for weight updates during optimization. Controls how much model weights change per gradient step. Set lower for RL (e.g., 1e-5) to avoid policy collapse; higher for SFT/DPO (e.g., 1e-4).
learning_rate.hint: Must be a value between 1e-07 and 0.001

lora_alpha.description: LoRA scaling factor. The effective learning rate for LoRA adapters scales as alpha/rank. Typically set to 2x the LoRA rank.

lora_rank.description: Number of trainable dimensions in the LoRA adapter. Higher values increase model capacity but use more memory.

lr_warmup_steps_ratio.description: Fraction of total training steps spent gradually increasing the learning rate from zero. Helps stabilize early training.
lr_warmup_steps_ratio.hint: Must be a value between 0 and 1

max_epochs.description: Number of complete passes through the entire training dataset. More epochs allow the model to learn patterns more thoroughly but increase training time and risk of overfitting.
max_epochs.hint: Must be a value between 1 and 100

max_prompt_length.description: Maximum number of tokens reserved for the prompt/input portion of each sequence. Cannot exceed the recipe's baked-in maximum.

max_response_length.description: Maximum number of tokens allowed for the generated response portion. Cannot exceed the recipe's baked-in maximum.
max_response_length.hint: Must be a value between 100 and 200000

min_lr.description: Lowest learning rate the scheduler decays to during training. Prevents the learning rate from dropping to zero in later steps.
min_lr.hint: Must be a value between 0.0 and 1.0

rollout_n.description: Number of candidate responses generated per prompt during training. More samples improve training quality but increase compute time.

rollout_temperature.description: Controls the diversity of generated responses during training rollouts. Higher values produce more varied outputs.
rollout_temperature.hint: Must be a value between 0.01 and 2.0

temperature.description: Sampling temperature for evaluation and generation. Higher values increase output randomness/diversity; lower values make outputs more deterministic.
temperature.hint: Must be a value between 0.0 and 2.0

train_val_split_ratio.description: Fraction of the dataset allocated to training versus validation. For example, 0.9 means 90% training and 10% validation.
train_val_split_ratio.hint: Must be a value between 0.0 and 1.0

use_kl_loss.description: Adds a penalty that keeps the training policy close to the reference policy. Disable to rely onclipping alone for training stability.

warmup_steps.description: Absolute number of training steps over which the learning rate linearly warms up from 0 to the target value.
warmup_steps.hint: Must be a value between -1 and 100

weight_decay.description: L2 regularization coefficient applied to model weights during optimization. Helps prevent overfitting by penalizing large weights.
